title: 1952 AHSME Problem 49
statement: In the figure, \(CD,\) \(AE,\) and \(BF\) are one-third of their respective sides. It follows that \(AN_2:N_2N_1:N_1D=3:3:1,\) and similarly for lines \(BE\) and \(CF.\) Then the area of triangle \(N_1N_2N_3\) is:

solutions.text:
Use \(A=(0,1),\) \(B=(0,0),\) \(C=(1,0).\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} D&=\left(\frac23,0\right),\\ E&=\left(\frac13,\frac23\right),\\ F&=\left(0,\frac13\right). \end{aligned} \] Intersecting \(AD,BE,CF\) in pairs gives \[ \begin{aligned} N_1&=\left(\frac47,\frac17\right),\\ N_2&=\left(\frac27,\frac47\right),\\ N_3&=\left(\frac17,\frac27\right). \end{aligned} \] The determinant area formula gives \[ \begin{aligned} [N_1N_2N_3]&=\frac1{14},\\ [ABC]&=\frac12. \end{aligned} \] Hence \(\frac{[N_1N_2N_3]}{[ABC]}=\frac{1}{7}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Area ratios are affine-invariant, so choose convenient coordinates for triangle \(ABC\)
Locate \(D,E,F\) by the one-third conditions, intersect the three cevians, and compare the two areas with determinants
